skill.name: web-design-guidelines
skill.description: Review UI code against Web Interface Guidelines for accessibility, UX, and interface quality.
skill.summary: Audits UI code against Web Interface Guidelines for accessibility and design quality.
skill.author: antfu

security_audit.summary: The external-command alerts are false positives caused by Markdown backticks and fenced code formatting. The hardcoded URL is a real low-severity network dependency, and the skill also delegates review behavior to mutable remote content from the main branch.

remediation.suggestion: Pin the guidelines URL to a reviewed commit SHA or vendor the guideline text into the skill release.
Keep output format and safety boundaries in local reviewed instructions, and treat fetched guidelines as reference material only.

static_findings.snippet: 4. Output findings in the terse `file:line` format

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 19 uses inline Markdown code around the text file:line to describe an output format. There is no shell interpreter, script, or executable command.
Line 25 opens a fenced Markdown block that displays a URL. It is documentation formatting, not Ruby or shell backtick execution.

Line 26 hardcodes a raw GitHub URL, and nearby instructions tell the agent to fetch it before each review. This is a real external network dependency, although the target is a public guideline document.

semantic_findings.title: Mutable Remote Instructions Control Reviews
semantic_findings.description: The skill tells the agent to fetch fresh guidelines and use the fetched content as the rules and output instructions. Because the URL tracks the main branch, remote changes can alter behavior after marketplace review.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The local instructions explicitly delegate rule and output behavior to fetched content. No malicious local text was found, so this is a supply-chain prompt-control risk rather than confirmed abuse.

content.value_statement: Teams need fast, consistent checks for accessibility, UX, and interface quality. This skill reviews UI code against Web Interface Guidelines and reports focused file-line findings.
actual_capabilities: Fetches the latest Web Interface Guidelines before a review.
Reviews user-selected files or patterns for guideline compliance.
Checks accessibility, usability, and interface design concerns.
Reports findings in a concise file-line format.
Asks which files to review when no target is provided.
limitations: Requires network access to fetch the guideline source.
Depends on the current content of an external main branch URL.
Reviews source files and cannot fully replace browser-based testing.
Needs clear file paths or patterns for focused results.

use_cases.title: Pre-merge UI Review
use_cases.description: Review changed frontend files before merging a pull request.

use_cases.title: Accessibility Triage
use_cases.description: Find likely accessibility issues in components before manual testing.

use_cases.title: Design Quality Audit
use_cases.description: Check product screens for guideline drift and inconsistent interface patterns.

prompt_templates.title: Review One Component
prompt_templates.prompt: Review src/components/Button.tsx against the Web Interface Guidelines.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review for one known file

prompt_templates.title: Check A Feature Area
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit the files under src/features/checkout for accessibility and UX issues.
prompt_templates.scenario: Focused review for a product flow

prompt_templates.title: Review Changed UI Files
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the changed frontend files in this branch and report only guideline violations.

prompt_templates.title: Prioritize Release Blockers
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit src/app and src/components, group findings by severity, and highlight issues that should block release.

output_examples.input: Review a navigation component for guideline compliance.
output_examples.output: Reports concise file-line findings for navigation clarity, keyboard access, focus handling, and responsive behavior.

output_examples.input: Audit checkout UI files before a pull request merge.
output_examples.output: Lists actionable issues tied to specific files and lines, with emphasis on accessibility and user flow problems.

output_examples.input: Check a design system component folder.
output_examples.output: Identifies inconsistent patterns, missing states, and guideline mismatches that affect reusable components.

best_practices: Provide narrow file paths or patterns to keep findings specific.
Run the review before visual QA so code issues are easier to fix.
Validate important findings with manual browser and accessibility testing.
anti_patterns: Do not use it as the only accessibility gate for production releases.
Do not review the entire repository when only one UI flow changed.
Do not ignore the fetched guideline version when comparing repeat audits.

faq.question: What does this skill review?
faq.answer: It reviews UI source files against Web Interface Guidelines for accessibility, UX, and interface quality.

faq.question: Does it need internet access?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill instructs the agent to fetch the latest guideline text before each review.

faq.question: Can it review multiple files?
faq.answer: Yes. You can provide a file path, folder, or pattern for the review target.

faq.question: Does it run a browser test?
faq.answer: No. It reviews files through the agent and does not perform automated browser testing by itself.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: How should I handle findings?
faq.answer: Treat findings as review guidance, then verify important issues in the running interface.
